name: Does the kitchen work triangle still matter in a tiny kitchen, or is that outdated advice?

mainEntity.name: Does the kitchen work triangle still matter in a tiny kitchen, or is that outdated advice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep the refrigerator, range, and sink in a workable relationship, but do not force a textbook triangle into a room with awkward doors or limited width. In a small kitchen, uninterrupted counter landing space, clear drawer operation, and a short path between preparation and cooking may matter more. Elite Remodeling & Design can test alternative layouts against your actual room dimensions and household routines. Key factors include whether one person or several cook, where groceries enter, appliance opening directions, and the location of trash and dishwasher. Sketch your normal meal-preparation route before the consultation. Choose the arrangement that reduces crossing and backtracking, not the one that looks best on paper.
acceptedAnswer.description: The principle still helps, but a rigid triangle is not required. In a small kitchen, prioritize short preparation routes, usable counter landing areas, clear appliance doors, and minimal crossing based on how your household actually cooks.
